citations.claim: energy after ceiling bounce slightly above E0
energy jumps +58J during free fall with no wall contact
speed increases from 41.68 to 44.99 while falling, faster than g*dt allows

counterfactual.change: changed only dt from 0.0287473 to 0.005 (single field) keeping steps=3, same body/gravity; smaller dt eliminates integration error and energy stays below limit, proving large-dt gravity integration causes the violation

explanation: Shrunk single-body free-fall with elastic ceiling bounce (e=1) and large dt=0.0287 shows monotonic energy gain without controller work: gravity integration with semi-implicit Euler and ~40 substeps per step adds ~1J after bounce then ~58J and ~61J on next two free-fall steps. Energy rises from E0 971.965 to 1092.714 at step 3, exceeding the 10%+5J allowance (1074.16). Reducing dt to 0.005 eliminates drift, and zero-gravity also eliminates it, confirming numerical energy creation by the integrator under large dt + gravity, especially after restitution-handling, not external work.
vision_note: Steps 0-3 show a single blue body near the top edge falling smoothly downward under gravity with no visible wall contact, penetration or tunneling. No sudden jump or explosion is apparent; the motion looks like normal free-fall, so an energy-bound violation is not visually obvious.
